title: Standby node proofing and failover throttle orchestration
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement an orchestration layer that (1) performs verifiable proofing of standby/private nodes (on-prem and VPC) when they enter 'standby' mode, (2) enforces regional failover throttles/fencing to satisfy residency SLAs, and (3) bundles immutable evidence artifacts for automated audit reporting. This ticket covers runtime gating, evidence bundler, and the failover throttle controller used by the residency orchestrator.
acceptance_criteria: Standby node proofing: newly decommissioned or standby nodes produce a signed provenance bundle (node id, geolocation assertion, KMS-signed timestamp) and are discoverable via the residency catalog API

Failover throttle: regional failover controller can be configured with policy windows (max parallel evacuations, time-based gates) and prevents automatic routing changes that would violate residency constraints

Evidence bundler: for any failover event, a single export contains the node bundles, routing decisions, and telemetry traces and is consumable by the Compliance export consumer (S3/GCS/secure artifact store)
Automated tests: unit and integration tests covering proof bundle generation, throttle behavior under simulated load, and evidence export checksum verification
Rollout plan: feature flag gated rollout to Private customers and smoke-tested against a staging VPC with synthetic residency constraints
No regression: existing hosted API traffic unaffected; dedicated nodes continue current behavior unless flag enabled
technical_notes: Proofing artifacts format: JSON-LD envelope, compact SHA256 checksums, KMS signature field (compatible with existing audit_verifier service)
Throttle controller: token-bucket style limiter per-region + global emergency circuit-breaker. Config stored in config-service with RBAC write controls
Integration points: residency-orchestrator (control plane), node-agent (bundle uploader), audit_exporter (packager), routing-proxy (to apply throttles)
Failure modes: if proof artifact upload fails, node remains quarantined and cannot be marked standby; operator alert emitted
Telemetry: expose Prometheus metrics: standby_proofs_total, failover_throttle_evaluations, throttle_blocked_events, evidence_exports_total
Data retention: proof bundles retained per-customer configured retention window; metadata indexed for fast search but payloads stored encrypted in artifact-store
test_plan: Unit: proof bundle generation with simulated KMS signer; signature verification against audit_verifier
Integration: staged failover in isolated VPC with 3 regions, assert throttle prevents >2 simultaneous evacuations
E2E: trigger scheduled evacuation, validate evidence export is generated and checksum matches uploaded artifact
Chaos: simulate network partition between node-agent and artifact-store and assert appropriate alarms and quarantine behavior
rollout_plan: Feature flag default OFF for all customers
Enable in staging tenant and run synthetic evacuation tests (2 days)
Invite 1 pilot Private/VPC customer -> monitor for 1 week; run compliance export checks
Gradual enable in 5% of Private fleets -> 25% -> 100% if no regressions
Communicate to customer success + SOC before every major step
migration_notes: Backward compatibility: older private nodes that lack node-agent v2 will be marked 'unproven' and excluded from automatic evacuation until upgraded
Data cleanup: a one-time job will tag legacy proof artifacts with migrated=true and move them to the new artifact-store path
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: KMS signing latency could delay node standby -> Mitigation: asynchronous signing with 'pending' state and operator override path
Risk: Overly strict throttle prevents urgent evacuations -> Mitigation: emergency eviction policy requiring human approval and audit log
Risk: Large evidence bundles could exceed artifact-store upload limits -> Mitigation: chunked uploads with manifest file and proof-of-completeness checksum
